transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Maya brings a torn red kite to her grandfather Arun's kitchen table.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: She found it in a cupboard. Can we buy a new one? Maya asks.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: We could, Arun says. But I made this one with your mother when she was your age.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Maya looks at the crooked wooden frame. Now she understands why Arun kept the old kite.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I thought the tear meant it was finished, she says. Arun points to a piece of yellow paper.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: A patch can give it another chance, he says. Would you like to help me mend it?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Maya takes the paper. Together, they plan where the patch should go, one corner at a time.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: When it flies again, Maya says, it will have a little bit of both of us.

facts.text: Maya and Arun sit at a kitchen table with a torn red kite, a spool of string and yellow paper.
Maya found the kite in a cupboard and asks about buying a new one.
Arun made this kite with Maya's mother when her mother was Maya's current age.
Maya understands that Arun kept the kite because of its connection to her mother.
Maya thought the tear meant the kite was finished; Arun points to yellow paper.
Arun suggests a patch and invites Maya to mend the kite with him.
Maya and Arun plan the repair together.
Maya says that when the kite flies again it will have a little bit of both of them. The story does not show it flying.
